newsitem.title: USA: Minn. Governor signs $6.7 bln education bill.
newsitem.headline: Minn. Governor signs $6.7 bln education bill.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson signed a two-year $6.7 billion education funding plan Monday that resolves a dispute with lawmakers over tuition tax credits.

Legislators had adopted the plan during a special session last week. Carlson had vetoed the entire elementary and secondary education funding package earlier in June because it lacked $150 million of tax credits he had proposed.
The overall spending plan increases education funding 19 percent and provides $75 million of additional tax credits each year if November revenue forecasts show money is available.

Current education deductions will be increased by 2.5 times and will now include private school tuition, computer software and hardware, transportation expenses, education summer school, textbooks, equipment, tutoring and instructional materials.
The plan also expands working family credits and introduces a refundable education tax credit for families with incomes of $33,500 or less beginning in the 1998 tax year.
The new refundable credit would provide $1,000 per child and up to $2,000 per family and applies to all items under the tax deduction except tuition for private schools.
